CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: Moderate generic software-supply-chain overlap, but the single host-local gate spanning three acquisition surfaces with revision-bound evidence, exact exceptions, keyed single-use permits, and crash-safe journal/projection recovery is materially differentiated.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: scanner unavailable or scanner database revision changes
mutable tag/version resolving to a new digest
stale, malformed, or partially written cache evidence
permit tamper, expiry, replay, restart, and concurrent consumption
crash between journal durability and derived projection update
malformed/incomplete journal tail versus corruption in durable history
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Make package, container, and build-dependency acquisition converge on one host-local Go admission boundary that enforces artifact identity, source trust, current vulnerability evidence, scoped exceptions, permit integrity, and durable decision state.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: ArtifactGuard already exposes evaluate and verify-permit entrypoints, package/container/dependency manager profiles, policy/scanner/exception inputs, reusable scan evidence, permits, and caller-owned durable state with a decision journal and derived latest-decision view.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: Strong: the engineering objective and material invariants fit comfortably within the <=20-bullet Edition-3 instruction shape, while architecture, CLI, state formats, and operational semantics can remain in normal solver-visible technical docs.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: repairing only high-level package managers while low-level or dependency managers bypass the shared trust boundary
making cache entries time-fresh without binding them to immutable digest plus active policy/scanner revisions
tightening exception expiry while still allowing exceptions to bypass source/digest/evidence prerequisites
keying permit signatures without binding request, instance, digest, policy, expiry, and durable single use
writing the latest-decision projection before the authoritative journal is durable
rejecting sequential replay while allowing two concurrent consumers to win the same permit
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: preserve artifactguard evaluate and verify-permit interfaces and documented exit behavior
keep cache and exceptions operational rather than disabling them
do not rewrite supplied policy, scanner, or exception fixtures
preserve valid existing audit history and healthy cached evidence
retain stateless permit-verification compatibility while making stateful verification durable and single-use
CANDIDATES.REASONING_CHAIN: normalize acquisition context -> establish trusted source and immutable digest -> select fresh scanner/cache evidence -> evaluate vulnerability threshold and exact exception -> issue or verify bound permit -> atomically journal decision/consumption -> recover and project durable state
CANDIDATES.REQUIRED_END_STATE: Every acquisition surface applies the same prerequisite trust and immutable-identity rules, uses only current artifact/policy/scanner evidence, limits exceptions to the exact vulnerability scope, issues and consumes exact-scope keyed permits safely, and commits restart-safe ALLOW/DENY history before completion.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: durable journal, projection, corruption handling, and idempotency
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: VERY_HIGH: the work is a coherent strict-scale security/state-model completion spanning differentiated manager normalization, policy, evidence/cache, exception, permit, replay, journal, recovery, and CLI responsibilities. Those coupled boundaries naturally produce broad normal, rejection, stale-state, restart, corruption, idempotency, and concurrency behavior without unrelated padding.

CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: Higher: cache invalidation and scanner freshness are common security-gate themes, making this less distinctive as a standalone strict-scale work package.
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Rework local artifact evidence into a revision-aware reconciliation subsystem that safely transitions cached scan state across policy and scanner-database changes while preserving availability and fail-closed behavior.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: The runtime already has scanner fixtures, reusable evidence, policy versions, scanner database revisions, a caller-owned state directory, and evaluation paths across multiple acquisition surfaces.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: Strong and concise, but its narrower scope leaves substantial existing permit/exception/journal behavior mostly as preservation-only context.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: fail-closed scanner path that breaks valid fresh-cache reuse
CANDIDATES.REASONING_CHAIN: resolve immutable artifact -> identify active revisions -> choose scanner versus cache -> validate freshness -> persist evidence atomically -> evaluate -> recover state after interruption
CANDIDATES.REQUIRED_END_STATE: Cached evidence is reusable only for the exact immutable artifact and active revisions, scanner outages never convert unknown state into clean evidence, partial writes and stale state are rejected safely, and restart recovery converges without losing valid history.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: MEDIUM_HIGH: technically coherent and stateful, but narrower than the full admission package and at greater risk of needing artificial breadth to sustain the strict profile by itself.

CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: Moderate: durable authorization ledgers are familiar, though permit consumption plus crash-safe journal/projection coupling is nontrivial.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: complete final journal record without newline
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Harden ArtifactGuard's authorization and persistence plane so allow permits are cryptographically bound and single-use while every policy decision is durably, idempotently recoverable across crashes and concurrent consumers.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: ArtifactGuard already issues permits, exposes verify-permit, stores decision state under a caller-provided state directory, and maintains an authoritative journal plus a derived latest-decision projection.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: Strong, but would underuse the existing three-surface policy architecture and narrow the requested software-supply-chain domain to authorization/persistence mechanics.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: sequential replay rejection without concurrent exclusion
tail repair that truncates valid committed records
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: do not alter deterministic input fixtures
CANDIDATES.REASONING_CHAIN: canonicalize authorization scope -> sign -> verify exact binding -> lock/consume replay state -> journal decision -> fsync authoritative state -> advance projection -> recover and deduplicate on restart
CANDIDATES.REQUIRED_END_STATE: Permits are keyed, exact-scope, unexpired, and atomically consumed when stateful verification is requested; authoritative ALLOW/DENY history is crash-safe, projection state never leads the journal, and recovery preserves valid committed history while rejecting corruption.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: HIGH for stateful/concurrency depth but still narrower than WP1; it leaves manager/source/evidence/exception admission policy outside the main change and therefore has less organic behavioral breadth.

outputs.DUPLICATE_RISK_NOTES: Nearest generic patterns are artifact admission, vulnerability-cache freshness, and signed authorization tokens; the recommended package is differentiated by enforcing all three acquisition surfaces through one stateful host-local boundary whose evidence, exception, permit, replay, and crash-recovery semantics interact.
outputs.WHY_THIS_ONE: WP1 is the only candidate that uses the inherited three-surface ArtifactGuard architecture as one coherent production security work package rather than carving out a narrower subsystem. It naturally couples trust normalization, immutable identity, revision-aware evidence, exception ordering/scope, permit security, replay concurrency, durable journal ordering, recovery, and CLI compatibility, giving the strict profile broad behavioral depth and realistic partial-fix traps without filler.
